text:
ConocoPhillips gained 0.65% today, a modest move that fits into a broader two-week rally of nearly 6%. The gain came as oil prices edged lower on news of renewed U.S.-Iran peace efforts, which reduced concerns about Middle East supply disruptions—counterintuitively, this easing of geopolitical tension can support energy stocks by removing the wild-card risk premium from prices and allowing investors to focus on earnings fundamentals instead of worst-case scenarios.

The company is riding a wave of strong oil prices: U.S. crude is trading at $103 per barrel while global oil sits at $123, both well above historical averages. With Big Oil earnings season underway, the stock has been climbing steadily over the past two weeks, though today's gain was measured. The disconnect between global and U.S. oil prices—a roughly $20 spread—reflects geopolitical and logistics complexity, but both levels remain favorable for a major oil producer's profitability.
